I'd like to make a `Number Field` that can also evaluate equations using [math.js](https://mathjs.org/index.html).

"5 + 20" -> "25"

"sqrt(16)" -> "4"

Is this possible with the current `Number Field`? I can't seem to find a way to let the input accept special characters. I'd also need to extend the parse function to attempt to evaluate with math.js before the base-ui parse function takes over.

Fixes #4809.

Follow-up to #4806.

`SelectRoot` and `AriaCombobox` use the same hidden-input autofill pattern that
`OTPFieldRoot` used before #4806, but their hidden-input `onChange` handlers
still only guard `defaultPrevented`, not `disabled || readOnly`.

This PR applies the same locked-state guard to those remaining handlers.

`AriaCombobox` is the shared root used by:
- `Combobox.Root` (`selectionMode='single' | 'multiple'`)
- `Autocomplete.Root` (`selectionMode='none'`)

## What changed

- `SelectRoot.tsx`: hidden-input `onChange` guard now matches OTP's
- `AriaCombobox.tsx`: same one-line guard update
- Regression tests added for:
  - `Select`
  - `Combobox` (`selectionMode='single'`)
  - `Autocomplete` (`selectionMode='none'`)

Each regression test fires `change` on the hidden input and verifies that no public state change happens while `readOnly` or `disabled`.

No public API change.

Addressed the NumberField gap in 5b5865dc5.

- Added the same locked-state guard to NumberField's hidden input autofill path: `defaultPrevented || disabled || readOnly` now returns early and calls `event.preventBaseUIHandler?.()` so Field validation handlers do not clear existing errors while locked.
- Added NumberField regression coverage for `readOnly` and `disabled`, both inside and outside `Field.Root`.
- Reduced the existing Select and Combobox locked-state regression tests to table-driven coverage while preserving the inside/outside Field assertions.

I considered adding `readOnly={readOnly}` to NumberField's hidden input for consistency with Select/Combobox/OTPField, but kept this as a handler guard only. Unlike those text hidden inputs, NumberField uses a `type="number"` hidden input with native `min`/`max`/`step`/`required` validation; setting `readOnly` on the input would bar it from constraint validation and could silently allow invalid read-only values through form submission.

Verified with:

- `pnpm test:jsdom NumberField --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom Select --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom Combobox --no-watch`

Fixes #4828.

Follow-up to #4806 and #4810.

#4806 added a locked-state guard to OTP Field's hidden autofill input, but when the component is wrapped in `Field.Root`, the merged Field validation `onChange` can still run after the OTP Field handler returns. This can clear existing Form errors or commit validation while the field is `readOnly` or `disabled`.

This PR calls `event.preventBaseUIHandler?.()` before returning from the locked hidden-input autofill path, matching the Select, Combobox, and NumberField handling from #4810.

The tests now cover the locked-state matrix for hidden-input autofill:

- `readOnly` / `disabled`
- inside `Field.Root` / outside `Field.Root`

The outside-Field cases keep asserting that OTP Field public callbacks are not called. The inside-Field cases additionally assert that existing `Field.Error` content is preserved.

Verified with:

- `pnpm test:jsdom OTPField --no-watch`
- `pnpm typescript`

Cleanup pass following #4911, which fixed double validation for Checkbox, Switch, and Slider. This removes the shared input-specific validation prop helper so each field-aware control validates the semantic value it owns.

## Changes

- Removed `getInputValidationProps` from the field validation context.
- Moved plain string input validation into `Field.Control`.
- Updated Select, Combobox, NumberField, and OTP hidden inputs to use validation props without a default `onChange`.
- Added Field.Control regression tests for one on-change validation call and for clearing a prefilled required value.

## Behavior note

`Field.Control` now marks a prefilled required control invalid immediately when the user clears it in `validationMode="onChange"`, because clearing the value is treated as a dirty user edit.

1. Made it possible to prevent default Base UI logic by calling `preventBaseUIHandler` in event handlers (fixes #1441) ([before](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/shy-fire-rpfyxk?file=%2Fsrc%2FApp.tsx%3A13%2C22&workspaceId=ws_QAeLcZEcDnfGaFA47etEUH) / [after](https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/friendly-rgb-28p6wf?file=%2Fsrc%2FApp.tsx%3A10%2C62)).
2. Fixed the behavior of disabled non-interactive triggers (i.e., `<Menu.Trigger disabled render={<span />} />`). Clicking on such a trigger used to open the menu anyway. ([before](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/gallant-agnesi-f98dt3?file=%2Fsrc%2FApp.tsx%3A7%2C16&workspaceId=ws_QAeLcZEcDnfGaFA47etEUH) / [after](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/hardcore-framework-rfxjvv?file=%2Fsrc%2FApp.tsx%3A10%2C22&workspaceId=ws_QAeLcZEcDnfGaFA47etEUH))
3. Removed `mergeReactProps` calls where they were not necessary.
4. Removed the `disabled` attribute from `SubmenuTrigger`. The submenus should be disabled by setting `disabled` on the Root part.
5. Updated the [fully featured menu experiment](https://deploy-preview-1445--base-ui.netlify.app/experiments/menu/menu-fully-featured) to cover more cases.

The main problem in 1. was that event handlers returned from Floating UI's `useInteractions` didn't respect preventBaseUIHandler as they have their own prop merging logic.
Instead of using these prop getters directly, I now call them without arguments and pass the result to our `mergeReactProps` function.

Another issue I found was that we had to nest `mergeReactProps` calls and props getters, such as `getButtonProps(mergeReactProps(external, internal))`. In some cases this was confusing and error-prone (point 2.), so I updated `mergeReactProps` to accept either props directly or a props getter function.

When a function is provided to `mergeReactProps`, it will be called with all the props defined to the right of it, so `mergeReactProps(obj1, obj2, fn, obj3, obj4)`, will be equivalent to `mergeReactProps(obj, obj2, fn(mergeReactProps(obj3, obj4)))`.
I assume that in such cases it is the props getter functionality to merge incoming and internal props and prevent default logic if needed.

Fixed the `mergeReactProps` utility to handle event handlers that don't have the event as the first parameter. It now checks if the parameter is an object and contains the `nativeEvent` field before adding the `preventBaseUIHandler` method.

Additionally, I refactored the implementation to be more readable.

Fixes #1430

## Summary

Reduces shared bundle cost across the popup, focus-management, and selector paths used by many Base UI components.

This PR keeps the measurable wins from the internal `tabbable` helper and the plain-vs-memoized selector split, trims shared utility code used across popup-heavy components, and avoids the broader unverified `@base-ui/utils/store/...` import-path churn so store consumers continue to use the standard barrel entrypoint.

## Changes

- Replace the external `tabbable` dependency with a smaller internal helper and add focused regression coverage for shadow DOM, `details`, hidden controls, radio groups, inert content, and embedded focusable elements.
- Split plain and memoized selector helpers so entrypoints that only need plain selectors do not pull memoized selector overhead.
- Remove redundant non-reactive Combobox store selector subscriptions.
- Simplify shared render, transition, animation, popup, and store utilities used across multiple components.

## Notes

- The latest published bundle bot result on this PR reports `@base-ui/react` down by `4.33 KB` parsed and `1.57 KB` gzip versus `master`.
- Latest targeted perf checks in exported production builds still favor the PR head on `combobox-perf` and `select-perf`, while a Chromium `100`-slider mount check is effectively flat versus `master`.
- Broader popup-route perf has been mixed rather than uniformly better, so this PR should be understood primarily as a shared bundle-size reduction with targeted runtime wins, not as an across-the-board popup perf improvement.

## Codex Review

### Overview
This PR still delivers a real shared bundle-size win on the latest rebased head by shrinking the common popup, focus, and selector paths without leaning on speculative import churn. After rechecking the full branch and the follow-up fixes on the current head, I did not find a remaining correctness or runtime regression worth blocking on.

### Findings (None)
No blocking issues found in this patch.

### Confidence: 4/5
High confidence from a fresh branch-wide pass plus new bundle snapshots against current `master`, exported-production popup benchmarks, a Chromium `Radio` / `Checkbox` / `Tabs` sanity pass, and focused local verification of the lint/test regressions that were still present on the previous pushed head.

# Feature request

**NOTE:** I am aware that Base-UI refers to Dialogs for non-gesture controlled drawers, but I believe this request is different enough and has its own use cases.

## Summary

Add a `dismissible` prop to manually control whether the Drawer can be closed via gestures, backdrop click, or Escape key. This would make it possible for drawers to temporarily act like a non-dismissible alert. This could also be described as a bug, as the request stems from an issue while working with [Motion](https://motion.dev/) draggable elements inside of a drawer component, where the two elements end up fighting over gesture controls. 

## Examples in other libraries

Vaul by Emil Kowalski, a popular drawer library for React, has this prop: [Other - non-dismissible](https://vaul.emilkowal.ski/other#non-dismissible)

## Motivation

In my case this forces the drawer to become non-gesture controlled while a drag is occurring, preventing accidental gesture dismissals of the drawer when not desired. This could also be used for forcing the drawer to stay open for some amount of time. This also just grants more manual control over how the drawer behaves when desired.

## Example

I have made a crude patch to get the desired behavior. Notice the buggy behavior in the example below where the drawer follow my cursor even after the drag has begun:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dcd051d2-5c35-496d-b116-243df92ea975

Implementing a new "dismissible" prop into the drawer I am able to early return the events. **Note:** shouldn't this also be possible with `event.preventBaseUIHandler();`? Doesn't seem like that works though. The only slight issue with this is the return transition as the drawer gets offset from the initial touch event, but then afterwards is forced back to its initial resting position. Here is the behavior I somewhat desire with this feature request:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c605d99d-fa3c-4dc5-8da9-38162069314e

## Alternative API changes

Instead of having a `dismissible` prop, this could also just be a `disableDrag` or `disableGestures` prop, since it is already possible to intercept final dismissals through the `onOpenChange` callback.

# Feature request ## Summary I'd like to request support for a built-in way to render a "Select all visible" option so selecting mutlitple options can be done with 1 click on top pinned item in Combobox list. My suggestion is to add new components - ListHeader and SelectAll so usage may look like this: ```tsx {(item) => ( {item.label} )} ``` ## Examples in other libraries [Prime React](https://primereact.org/multiselect/) ## Motivation I'm trying to create a combobox with top pinned option that changes selection for all visible options. I was able to achive that behaviour with controlled api and some additional context, but I think it would be nice to have same functionality out of the box and for uncontrolled component as well.

Thanks @aarongarciah — that makes sense, and sorry for opening the PR before aligning on the approach.

You’re right: keyboard navigation couldn’t reach the original `Combobox.SelectAll` because it was a separate `role="checkbox"` control outside the `role="listbox"`. I’ve updated the PR so `Combobox.SelectAll` is implemented as a `Combobox.Item` (same idea as the Stackblitz `Item` hack), placed as the first child inside `Combobox.List`, with `preventBaseUIHandler()` so the sentinel value isn’t added to the selection. Arrow keys + Enter now reach it, and there’s a test for that.

I also updated `Combobox.List` to allow a static `<Combobox.SelectAll />` sibling before the collection render function.

Prevent the outer tooltip from opening when the cursor is over an enabled nested tooltip trigger. When the outer tooltip is already open and the pointer moves onto a nested trigger, close it when the bubbling `mouseover` event reaches the outer trigger and detects a nested trigger target so that only the innermost tooltip is visible. Disabled nested triggers are excluded from detection so the parent tooltip still opens.

The close path is gated to hover-opened tooltips only — focus-opened tooltips remain visible until blur.

Closes #4499

This changes how custom event callbacks pass events.

Previously, the native event and reason would be passed like so:
```js
onOpenChange={(open, event, reason) => {}}
```

They would potentially be undefined.

Now, a `BaseUIEventDetails` object is passed as the second param, which contains `eventDetails.reason`, `eventDetails.event`, `eventDetails.cancel()` and `eventDetails.allowPropagation()`.

```js
onOpenChange={(open, details) => {}}
```

The `details` is always defined; the `event` falls back to `new Event('base-ui')` if it's triggered inside an effect or during render (rather than an event handler).

`.cancel()` cancels the event from having an effect while leaving the component uncontrolled (previously it needed to be controlled). You can also only cancel `.stopPropagation()` from being called: `.allowPropagation()`

(We can add `.allowDefault()` in the future if it becomes needed)

## Unified change reasons

Every component that has a `change` handler (e.g. `onOpenChange`, `onValueChange`) has an exported `ChangeEventReason` type and `ChangeEventData` (the second parameter)

For `onValueChange` callbacks and others which never passed a reason before, I've initialized the reason to `'none'`. We could supply reasons for these if they become necessary in the future

## Event narrowing

`data.event` is now narrowed to the correct type based on the `reason` string without needing to cast (e.g. `MouseEvent`) to access detailed properties

## Experiment

1. The 'B' tooltip doesn't hide when pressing the trigger (once it's open).
2. The 'I' tooltip doesn't stop propagation of `escape-key`

Will `event.preventBaseUIHandler()` remove Base UI side effects like this Esc propagation stopped?
https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/589511b4bf0836e01fd7706973469a12039abc51/packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useDismiss.ts#L192

My problem / use case:

I've got a non-modal dialog which I'd like it to close on Esc only if an element in the dialog is focused, otherwise keep the dialog open and use Esc in my own handler.

It's easy to keep the dialog open after Esc keypress, but I can't process Esc on my side because dialogs swallow Esc and it doesn't reach my event listener

(I have to say in most cases it's very appreciated that dialogs stop Esc propagation when I do want them to close the way it works by default, but when I want to prevent the default behavior, I want complete control over everything)
@vladmoroz we're discussing this now! We might allow passing options like `.preventBaseUIHandler({ stopPropagation: boolean })`

Great to hear that. So in this case would passing `true` mean that Base UI still stops propagation, or that I'm preventing Base UI from stopping propagation?
```
event.preventBaseUIHandler({ stopPropagation: true })
```

fwiw if I am down this route, I think I can stop propagation myself, and I guess it doesn't apply to all events (I assume only some stop propagation)

@vladmoroz would you prefer

`onOpenChange={(open, data) => {})`

Where `data.event` is the native event (and now `data.reason`)

or 

`onOpenChange={(open, event, data) => {})`

I've changed approach since cloning events is messy, we should avoid mutating native DOM events with custom properties.

The handler is now attached to data either way: `data.preventBaseUIHandler()`

We could attach the React event as `data.reactEvent` and keep `data.event` as native (not all events are from React props)

> I've changed approach since cloning events is messy, we should avoid mutating native DOM events with custom properties.
> The handler is now attached to data either way: data.preventBaseUIHandler()

Yeah I much prefer this, the contract is much clearer when the methods like this are on a separate object instead of sneaking it into the event. If you are sticking to `allowPreventDefault, allowStopPropagation`, would a boolean option for preventing the Base UI handler also work?

I don't care about React events vs native events too much, having access to the native event is enough for me personally.

The `OpenChangeReason`s do require the component to become controlled however as you need to prevent calling `setOpen(...)`

In https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/2382, we're exploring how to leave it uncontrolled (and call `event.preventBaseUIHandler()` to stop the handler)
